clue.text: Approaches very old people

definitions.meaning: ways of looking at or tackling a problem, viewpoints
the Germanic tribe who settled England in the fifth century and gave it its name

explanation.surface: Someone sidles up to the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: viewpoints taken on a question, and the ancient Germanic tribe that settled England.

clue.text: Erotic writer concerned with material

parts.note: Anaïs Nin, famous for her erotic fiction
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A writer of erotica is interested in fabrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a fine sheer fabric of silk or nylon, a kind of dress material.

clue.text: Pass through US city's ancient ground

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles; the 's joins it to what follows

indicators.note: ground as the past participle of grind: the letters of the word ancient are crushed and remade

explanation.surface: Someone travels through the ancient lands of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for land but is the past tense of grind, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To lancinate is to pierce or stab, so to go right through something.

clue.text: Describing eclipse, calls up astronaut

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole construction is read from the bottom upwards
describing in its geometric sense of drawing a line around, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
to cap is to outdo or surpass, as to eclipse is

explanation.surface: Someone describing an eclipse calls an astronaut on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing around; 'up' then reverses the whole result in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman is a popular term for a space traveller, synonym of astronaut.

clue.text: Sound of one feeding child an alternative to jelly

indicators.note: tells us to say the phrase out loud and take what it sounds like

parts.note: to dine a mite: feed (dine) one (a) small child (mite)

explanation.surface: Something sounding like a parent giving a toddler pudding instead of jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jelly' here is gelignite, an explosive, not a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly is slang for gelignite, an explosive, and dynamite is another explosive used in its place.

clue.text: Count bones, a hundred, and regularly upload

parts.note: Bones is the nickname of the doctor in Star Trek, so a doctor, DR
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the following word, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: An instruction to tally bones and upload the total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hundred' gives the A and the C separately: A, then C for one hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the vampire count of Bram Stoker's novel, a title of nobility.

clue.text: Turning 24, receive a piece of wisdom

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read in reverse order

parts.note: refers to the 24-across answer, a handgun, so a gun
to get is to receive

explanation.surface: Turning twenty-four, you receive some wise advice.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' looks like an age but points to another answer in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small valuable piece, as in a nugget of wisdom, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Tramp raised pack horse

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is lifted to read upwards

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A vagrant lifted a load onto a packhorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun for a vagrant but is the verb, to walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long way with heavy steps, which is what marching is.

clue.text: Arranged at Jarrow, new attack on Paris

indicators.note: letters arranged into a new order, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: An attack on the French capital was organised at Jarrow, a town in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the city but the Trojan prince who carried off Helen and was attacked by the Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks waged a long war on Troy, home of Paris, after he abducted Helen.

clue.text: Native American chief would never, never return

indicators.note: return means the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish chief or commander
D is the contracted form of would, as in I'd
no means not at all, never
a second no for the repeated never

explanation.surface: A tribal leader vowed that he would never come back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Onondaga are a people of the Iroquois Confederacy in New York State.

clue.text: Turn right and head north to find battle-axe

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
to head somewhere is to go there
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Directions: turn right and go north to locate a battle-axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battle-axe' is not a weapon but a formidable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle-axe and a gorgon are both insulting names for a fearsome, domineering woman.

clue.text: I will gather wood for burning

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
fir is a type of wood

explanation.surface: Someone promises to collect firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alight or blazing is burning, a plain synonym for the phrase.

clue.text: You and I must cross rather winding canals

indicators.note: to cross a thing here is to straddle it, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: you and I together are us

indicators.note: winding means twisting, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Two travellers must navigate some meandering waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canals' looks like waterways, but in anatomy a canal is a bodily duct.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a canal is any tube-like duct, and urethras are the ducts carrying urine.

clue.text: Clothes off, as rubber will do

parts.note: clothing is called wear, as in menswear
away means off, absent

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off, as a rubber-clad figure might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' here is an eraser, not latex clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is gradually rubbed down and lost in use, so it erodes over time.

clue.text: Stab snake, resulting in rash

parts.note: to give something a whirl is to have a stab, an attempt
to snake is to wind, follow a twisting course

explanation.surface: Stabbing a snake gives you a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective, hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a whirlwind romance, it means sudden and hasty.

clue.text: Go out and sell a winger

definitions.meaning: to peddle goods from door to door or in the street
a winged creature, a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A footballer playing on the wing goes out selling.
explanation.definitionFit: A street seller peddles goods, and a falcon-like bird of prey has wings.

clue.text: Mostly quick boxing to preserve fighter

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece is put inside the other
mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: hurried means quick
to can food is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A boxer who is quick is mostly able to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the final D of HURRIED; 'fighter' is the warplane, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawker Hurricane was a British fighter aircraft of the Second World War.

clue.text: Tyres may be so adapted, else burst right away

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged
away means removed, so the letter goes from the word

explanation.surface: Tyres that have been modified, or else they burst at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst right away' reads as 'burst immediately', but it is BURST losing R; the rest joins ELSE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern car tyres often have no inner tube, which describes such tyres exactly.

clue.text: Lacking Ecstasy, take glue

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to seize is to take
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone without drugs sniffs glue instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is a gelatinous sealant used as a weak glue on paper and plaster.

clue.text: I get upset about some paper round's starting point

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the short word is reversed

parts.note: CA is circa, about
a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

indicators.note: the starting point of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A paperboy gets annoyed about where their round begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one speaking, someone who gets things is the person who says they obtain.

clue.text: Murderer's caught fitting lead

indicators.note: caught means holding, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means fitting, suitable

explanation.surface: A killer has been apprehended through an appropriate lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead a team or ship is to skipper it; as a verb lead and skipper share a sense.

clue.text: Bite one pepper

parts.note: the bite in the air is its cold, a chill
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Take a bite of a single pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: The chilli is a hot capsicum, one kind of pepper.

clue.text: Becomes weary with joint chief?

parts.note: to flag is to tire
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A boss tires and has a bad hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's leading product or store is its main one, used attributively as principal.

clue.text: Place for one to return clothing

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: to put is to place
EG, for example, signals for one

explanation.surface: A place for someone to give back clothes, like a returns desk.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit, especially an unusual one, is informally called this.

clue.text: Is against equality, heading to the far right

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, moves to the far right end of the word

parts.note: a sexist opposes equality between the sexes

explanation.surface: A political charge that someone opposes equality and is lurching to the far right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far right' sounds political, but it means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to have being, so is and has being, lives on, are synonyms.

clue.text: An Irishman might say one can't polish this bronze?

indicators.note: in an Irish accent the th sound is softened, so the word is pronounced differently

parts.note: the proverb says you can't polish a turd

explanation.surface: An Irishman complaining he can't put a shine on a bronze piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronze' is not the metal but the medal for coming in after silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze medals go to the competitor finishing behind gold and silver, in that position.

clue.text: Weapon very good, many rounds

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

indicators.note: to round is to turn back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: A good firearm fires many rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like ammunition but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is a small firearm held in one hand, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Prayer and song after Cockney's own Mass

indicators.note: the song is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so have, meaning own, becomes 'ave
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A prayer and hymn after a Londoner's own church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin, known by its Latin opening words.

clue.text: Acceptance of aid not unusual when out of work

indicators.note: out of means outside, so the shuffled letters sit around the other piece
unusual means strange, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Accepting help is rare when you are unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of work' looks like unemployment but puts the anagram of AID NOT around OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking up an idea or plan is embracing it, so taking it on is acceptance.

clue.text: Still sad, yet bubbly

indicators.note: bubbly means fizzing, lively, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Still sad, yet bubbly: a mixed mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the adjective, motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless is stable and unmoving, the sense of still here.
